description:
FDB's recovery does essentially nothing to storage servers, and ours does a great deal. Verified in /Users/j5n/Workspace/foundationdb:

- The ENTIRE interaction is one key. ClusterRecovery.actor.cpp:1689-1697 sets \xff/lastEpochEnd, with the comment: 'This transaction sets \xff/lastEpochEnd, which the shard servers can use to roll back speculatively processed semi-committed transactions from the previous epoch. It also guarantees the shard servers and tlog servers eventually get versions in the new epoch.' Storage learns about the epoch IN-BAND, from the mutation stream.
- RecoveryState::STORAGE_RECOVERED (ClusterRecovery.actor.cpp:519-520) is a STATUS LABEL fired when !newState.oldTLogData.size() — old tlog generations were dropped because storage caught up. Recovery observes storage; it does not drive it.
- Recovery never READS from storage: it rebuilds txnStateStore by peeking the old log system (ClusterRecovery.actor.cpp:1111), then reads config/serverTags/localities from there. keyServersPrefix and serverKeysPrefix are metadata mutations (ApplyMetadataMutation.h:120-121), so routing lives in that log-replayed store.
- The recovery version comes from tlogs only — and we already match this (log_recovery_planning_phase.ex calculate_durable_version over log_recovery_info). No materializer gates it, so NONE of our materializer work is load-bearing for transaction-system correctness.

Bedrock's recovery, by contrast, re-locks and unlocks a materializer for EVERY data tag, picks one member per tag, seeds routing with it, and diffs the family into the persistence commit.

CHANGE: recovery stops at tag 0. Data-tag materializers become the distributor's exclusive concern.

WHAT GETS DELETED:
- prefer_family_named/3 (materializer_bootstrap_phase.ex) — and with it the PR #198 audit's finding #8 seam, where recovery's pick and the client-facing pick agreed only by construction. The seam disappears rather than staying patched.
- the data-tag ensure_materializers_for_shards loop
- shard_materializers beyond tag 0; the routing seed carries only what recovery actually established
- prior_materializer_refs as a recovery input
- persistence_phase's build_materializer_keys diff — making the DISTRIBUTOR the sole writer of the materializers/ family

WHO ALREADY DOES IT: the distributor's startup sweep reads both families, verifies every named member is in this epoch (adopt or heal), places placeholders for gaps, recruits, and monitors. That IS getInitialDataDistribution + teamTracker, and it runs after every recovery regardless. Recruitment.adopt/4 already locks at the epoch and unlocks at the worker's own durable version.

WHY IT IS SAFE — locked does not mean unreadable: olivine/server.ex's {:get, ...} and {:get_range, ...} handlers carry NO mode guard. Locking fences :ingest (server.ex:140) and :apply_transactions (server.ex:350) only. A locked materializer still answers reads at its durable version — FDB's model exactly, where locking fences the write path, not the read path.

HONEST COST: between recovery completing and the sweep adopting, data materializers are not PULLING, so reads needing versions past their durable point wait and time out into a client retry. Today's pre-unlock shrinks that window — but the window already exists for every replica recovery does not adopt (that is finding #8). This generalizes an existing hole and forces a real answer instead of relying on the pick agreeing.

DIVIDEND: the 'three components, three beliefs about who serves this shard' problem collapses to two with zero overlap — recovery owns the transaction system plus tag 0; the distributor owns the materializers/ family and elastic membership; the materializer learns in-band (bedrock-q67.21.6). And bedrock-q67.46's locality-aware placement gets exactly one owner.

ALSO SHRINKS THE CRITICAL PATH: combined with bedrock-q67.21.12, the recovery lock set drops from O(shards x replicas) to O(logs + tag-0 replicas), on the most latency-sensitive operation in the system.

DEPENDS ON: bedrock-q67.21.12 (recovery needs a deterministic tag-0 entry point before it can stop discovering everything else).
title: Recovery stops at tag 0: the distributor owns data-tag materializers
